resulting_evidence:
Recommended direction: **an editorial portfolio led by expressive type, asymmetric spacing, and a clear reading order.**

The host blocked the local read command, and no alternative local file reader is exposed. I couldn’t read Andino, Taste, or the supplied files, so this is a provisional direction based on your fixture summary—not a completed skill-based audit. Nothing was changed.

Use these implementation targets:

| Element | Direction |
|---|---|
| Existing fonts | Retain self-hosted families and available weights. Use the most expressive existing face for the headline; the most readable for supporting copy. |
| Main headline | Start with `font-size: clamp(3rem, 7vw, 7rem)`, `line-height: 1.02`, and `max-width: 14ch`. Adjust tracking after inspecting the actual face. |
| Supporting text | Use `1.125rem`, line-height `1.6`, and a measure of `48–60ch`. Keep the introduction noticeably quieter than the headline. |
| Desktop composition | Use a 12-column grid: headline across roughly eight columns, supporting information across four, aligned near the headline’s lower edge. |
| Page rhythm | Start with 24–64px fluid side gutters and 64–128px between major sections. Use whitespace and thin rules to establish structure. |
| Work section | If projects exist, give the leading project greater width, then use smaller entries with consistent titles and metadata. Preserve supplied content. |
| Mobile | Collapse to one column in source order; remove offsets and forced line breaks. Let the headline wrap naturally. |
| Motion | Keep content visible by default. Any optional transitions belong inside `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`; avoid entrance animation dependencies. |

For later verification, check 320px, 768px, and 1440px widths plus 200% zoom: no horizontal overflow, clipped glyphs, or overlapping text. Confirm local font loading, readable fallback fonts, visible keyboard focus, sufficient contrast, and fully usable content with reduced motion enabled.

**Next action:** inspect the supplied HTML and font declarations through an authorized local reader, then map these targets to its actual selectors and content.
